Under the theme "Standing with teachers: 60 years of protecting the profession, advancing its status and shaping our futures", the global celebration at UNESCO Headquarters will feature high-level discussions on protecting and advancing the status of the teaching profession, as well as the award ceremony for the ninth edition of the UNESCO-Hamdan Prize for Teacher Development. 225th session of the Executive Board 5-20 October 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France) The 225th session of UNESCO’s Executive Board will bring together representatives of Member States to consider a range of issues related to UNESCO’s programme, activities and governance. The session will examine reports and proposals and take decisions on matters within the Organization’s mandate. UNESCO Prize for Girls’ and Women’s Education 9 October 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), 6pm-8pm, Room I The event, organized to mark the International Day of the Girl (observed annually on 11 Oct.), will feature the award ceremony for the 2026 UNESCO Prize for Girls' and Women's Education, recognizing two laureates for their innovative contributions to advancing girls’ and women’s education. It will also include the launch of the 2026 Global Education Monitoring (GEM) Gender Report. 11th GEF International Waters Conference (IWC11) 19-22 October 2026 (Bali, Indonesia) The IWC11 will bring together governments, Global Environment Facility (GEF) Agencies, regional organizations, executing partners, scientific institutions, civil society and development partners to exchange knowledge and advance cooperation on shared freshwater and marine ecosystems. Conference of the Parties (COP) to the Convention on Biological Diversity 19-30 October 2026 (Yerevan, Armenia) The 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP 17) will be held in Yerevan. The COP is the governing body of the Convention, and advances implementation of the Convention through the decisions it takes at its periodic meetings. Biennale of Luanda - Pan African Forum for the Culture of Peace and Non-violence 2026 - 4th Edition 22-23 October (Luanda, Angola) Organized by the African Union, UNESCO and the Government of Angola, the Biennale aims to promote violence prevention and conflict resolution by encouraging cultural exchanges in Africa and intergenerational dialogue. Under the theme “Strengthening Water Governance in Africa as a tool for preventing, mediating, and resolving conflicts”, in harmony with the African Union theme for 2026, “Assuring Sustainable Water Availability and Safe Sanitation Systems to Achieve the Goals of Agenda 2063”, the Biennale will show how Africa’s history contributes to building a culture of peace through the development of shared narratives that foster a sense of citizenship and African belonging. In this context, water can also be highlighted as a vector for peace, dialogue and cooperation, by encouraging shared resource management. 18th Concert for Peace « United in Light » 23 October 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), 7:45pm-10pm, Room I The Franco-Korean cultural event, held since 2008, is founded on a constant conviction: that artistic creation can provide a space for encounter, fraternity and mutual understanding among peoples. It will bring together Korean and French artists, established professionals and emerging talents, for a programme in which dance, jazz and the human voice engage in dialogue. Global Media and Information Literacy Week 24-31 October 2026 Commemorated every year on 24-31 October, Global Media and Information Literacy Week is a major occasion for mobilizing worldwide stakeholders to raise awareness, increase national take-up and celebrate the progress achieved towards Media and Information Literacy for all. This year’s theme is “We All Play a Part – Media and Information Literacy for the People”. Women, Peace and Security - UNESCO/UN Women side event 27 October 2026 (UN HQ – New York) A high-level joint event of UNESCO and UN Women on the occasion of UN Women, Peace and Security Week, marking the 26th anniversary of UN Security Council Resolution 1325. The focus will be on the safety of women journalists. Promoting Human Creativity and the Diversity of Cultural Expressions in the Digital Environment – International Congress on AI and Culture 27 October 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), Room II Multi-stakeholder dialogue organized in the framework of the Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions. It will explore the transformations brought about by artificial intelligence (AI) and the digital environment, while contributing to reflections on UNESCO’s future action in this area, including diversity of cultural expressions, cultural and creative industries, artists and cultural professionals. 100th anniversary of start of the construction of the Republic Square, Yerevan 28 October-3 November 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), Rooms I, IV, Pas Perdus Hall 28/10 Scientific conference dedicated to the 150th birth anniversary of the Armenian linguist Hrachia Acharian (Room IV, 11am-1pm) 28/10-3/11 Exhibition of Traditional Costumes (Pas Perdus Hall, 9am - 5:30 pm) 29/10 Musical evening with pianist Vahagn Hayrapetyan and the "Hover" State Chamber Choir of Armenia (Room I, 7-8:30 pm). 5th edition of the Global Forum against Racism and Discriminations 29-30 October 2026 (The Hague, Netherlands) Building on previous editions, the Forum will focus on translating commitments into concrete action to advance racial justice, combat discrimination, and promote more inclusive and equitable societies. Taking place within the second International Decade for People of African Descent (2025-2034), the Forum will place a strong emphasis on advancing racial justice for people of African descent. Home President 43rd Session Documents Previous Sessions Secretariat The General Conference determines the policies and the main lines of work of the Organization Its duty is to set the programmes and the budget of UNESCO. It also elects the Members of the Executive Board and appoints, every four years, the Director-General. The working languages of the General Conference are Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish. The General Conference consists of the representatives of UNESCO's Member States. It meets every two years, and is attended by Member States and Associate Members, together with observers for non-Member States, intergovernmental organizations and non-governmental organizations (NGOs). Each country has one vote, irrespective of its size or the extent of its contribution to the budget. event_date_text: SOUTHMOD at 10: Evidence Before Action 14 September 2026, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia | Ten years after the launch of SOUTHMOD , UNU-WIDER brings together government officials, researchers, and members of the SOUTHMOD network to celebrate and reflect on the programme's achievements; and explore its future role in supporting evidence-based policymaking across the Global South. Drawing on a decade of experience, the event examines how tax-benefit microsimulation can help governments design more effective, equitable, and data-driven policies. Read more Can Africa escape the climate–conflict–poverty trap? 30 September 2026, Helsinki, Finland | Climate change increasingly reshapes development prospects around the world, but the risks are especially acute in countries where livelihoods remain closely tied to rain-fed agriculture, state capacity is limited, and conflict risk is already high. On 30 September 2026, distinguished economist Edward Miguel delivers WIDER Annual Lecture 30, Can Africa escape the climate–conflict–poverty trap? In this lecture, Edward Miguel examines how rising temperatures, economic stress, and armed conflict interact to produce a vicious cycle that threatens long-term development, with a particular focus on Africa.
